Arbiter Commander
My 5/5 with deathtouch and trample attacks. They block with a 2/2. How much damage can I assign to the player?
Arbiter's ruling Assign 1 to the blocker, 4 to the player.

Because your creature has deathtouch, any nonzero amount of damage is lethal damage for the purpose of assigning combat damage 702.2c. Trample lets you assign the rest to the defending player 702.19b.

  1. 1Assign 1 damage to the 2/2 blocker — lethal, given deathtouch.
  2. 2Assign the remaining 4 damage to the defending player.
  3. 3The blocker is destroyed as a state-based action once damage resolves.
Rules cited 510.1a 702.2c 702.19b

The rulebook is read first

Every question searches the parsed Comprehensive Rules and hands the matching passages to the model before a word of the answer is written.

Check the work

Every chip opens its rule

Rule numbers appear inline and in a Rules Cited strip. Click one and the rule text opens beside the ruling, so you can read the source yourself.

Oracle text

Cards are looked up live

Name a card and the Arbiter pulls its current Oracle text from Scryfall rather than reciting a printing it half-remembers.

The Arbiter

A judge for the table you actually play at

Describe the board state in your own words, pick the format the ruling should be made under, and send. You get a one-line verdict, the reasoning underneath it, and the rules it rests on.

Format-aware. The same board reads differently in Commander and in Pauper — the ruling knows which you asked about.

Card text on hover. Any card named in an answer opens its mana cost, type line, and Oracle text without leaving the thread.

Kept in the archive. Rulings are saved and grouped by day, so the argument you settled last week is still there next week.

Blood Moon after Urborg
Blood Moon resolves after Urborg is already out. What are my Swamps?
Arbiter Legacy
Arbiter's ruling Every land is a Mountain. Nothing is a Swamp.
Layer 4 applies both effects in timestamp order, so Blood Moon's type-setting overwrites the Swamp type Urborg granted 613.1d.

Brew with the rules lawyer already at the table

Put the list on the right, say what the deck is trying to do on the left. The builder answers with what to add, what to cut, and the reason for each — checked against the format you chose.

Legality is enforced, not assumed. Duplicates, banned cards, and names it doesn't recognise are flagged before the question is even sent.

From collection to finished list

Three moves, in the order you'd make them

I

Bring the list you already have

Import a CSV straight out of ManaBox, Moxfield, Archidekt, or Deckbox. Columns are matched by name, duplicate printings merge into one line with a summed count, and the file is parsed in memory and discarded — it is never written to disk.

Import CSV collection-2026-08.csv
98 cards imported · 3 duplicate printings merged
2 Rite of Replication 1 Anointed Procession 1 Parallel Lives
II

Let it check itself

The list validates as you type, against the format you picked. Banned cards are off by default — the builder will never recommend one unless you deliberately allow it.

Banned in Commander
Golos, Tireless Pilgrim

2 Rite of Replication — singleton format
Name not recognised
Sol Rong — kept in the list, not dropped
Allow banned cards Off by default.
III

Then argue about it

Say what the deck wants to do and it answers in adds, cuts, and reasons — the same cited voice as the Arbiter, pointed at your curve instead of your combat step.

Build notes Two more lands, four fewer six-drops.
  • •36 lands is the floor with a five-mana commander.
  • •Add a second wipe-proof payoff — you have one.
How a ruling is made
1

You describe the board

Plain language, whatever detail you have, under the format you're playing.

2

The rulebook is searched

The most relevant Comprehensive Rules passages are retrieved and handed over as evidence, with card text pulled in when you name one.

3

You get a verdict and its sources

One line of answer, the reasoning beneath it, and every rule number it used — openable, so you can check.
